newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 edges lower, Wall Street seen weak.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 edges lower, Wall Street seen weak.

text.p: Britain's leading share index was moderately lower on Monday ahead of an expected weaker start on Wall Street and tracking softer gilts and U.S. Treasury prices, traders said.
The FTSE 100 pulled back from above 4,900 points that was touched when heavyweight HSBC Holdings Plc posted a sparkling set of results.
By 1303 GMT, the blue chip index was off 12.6 points at 4,886.7, with declines leading advances by a 64 to 28 margin. The broader FTSE Mid-250 lost 1.9 points to 4,486.5.
"We're just drifting lower with the S&P futures and the market is generally cautious after Friday," one trader said.

Surprisingly strong economic data on Friday raised concerns the Federal Reserve might tighten credit, sending bond yields soaring. The Dow closed moderately after losing more than 100 points during the day.
The FTSE 100 sprung to life after HSBC said its pre-tax profit in sterling terms rose 13 percent to 2.623 billion pounds. It raised the interim dividend by 33 percent to 20 pence per share.
Shares in HSBC, which were up 58p at 22.51-1/2 stg, Lloyds TSB Plc and Standard Chartered Bank Plc were among the biggest gainers.
"The figures did a lot of improve the mood of the market, but in general people are still pretty cautious ahead of this (August 6-7 Bank of England) meeting," said one dealer.
The market already has factored in a base rate hike of 25 basis points, dealers said.
If the newly-independent central bank moves to raise rates this week, it would be the fourth in the past four months.
But FTSE futures turned back lower ahead of the U.S. open then hovered near unchanged, with the September contract posting a one-point gain to 4,880.
Dealers said they expected the market to remain thin and volatile ahead of the policy-setting meeting.

"We're steady enough because HSBC was the major set of figures today and they were good news," said another dealer. "On the other hand, it seems like everyone is expecting interest rates to go up this week."
Among other individual stocks, shares in British Airways Plc slid after the UK flag carries issued disappointing results.
BA posted a 46.7 percent rise in first-quarter pre-tax profit to 220 million stg, but that total was boosted by a 130 million stg gain on the sale of its US Airways stake.
The shares were off 23p to 617.
Shares in Pearson Plc advanced 28p to 694 after the media and leisure group reported a surge in interim profits and said it aimed to double the value of the company within the next five years.

The company, whose shares have been dismal underperformers since early June, issued an optimistic trading statement, with promises of further growth in revenues and operating profits in the second half.
Elsewhere, shares in United Utilities Plc and Wessex Water Plc fell as brokerage HSBC James Capel cut its rating on the stocks to "sell" from "hold", market sources said.
